_note: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7 (Landlord's responsibilities) read with § 47a-4(a)(1) (the tenant cannot waive statutory rights), retrieved verbatim from cga.ct.gov on 2026-06-05. The landlord's duty to maintain a habitable, code-compliant unit cannot be shifted wholesale onto the tenant or waived. status=draft-unverified.

rules.title: Tenant made responsible for all repairs / maintenance
rules.description: Under § 47a-7 the landlord must keep the premises fit and habitable and make necessary repairs; § 47a-4(a)(1) bars waiving that statutory protection. A clause shifting all repair/maintenance duty onto the tenant is unenforceable as to the landlord's non-waivable obligations. (The tenant remains responsible for damage they cause, § 47a-11.)
rules.tenant_explainer: Keeping the place livable — heat, hot water, plumbing, structural and code repairs — is your landlord's job, not yours. A lease making you responsible for 'all repairs' can't sign that duty away. You're still on the hook for damage you actually cause.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7(a)
citations.quote: A landlord shall: … (2) make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition, except where the premises are intentionally rendered unfit or uninhabitable by the tenant … (4) maintain in good and safe working order … all electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and other facilities … (6) supply running water and reasonable amounts of hot water at all times and reasonable heat.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(1) — waiver of statutory rights prohibited
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: (1) Agrees to waive or forfeit rights or remedies under this chapter ….

rules.title: "As-is" / waiver of the warranty of habitability
rules.description: Under § 47a-7 the landlord must keep the unit fit and habitable; § 47a-4(a)(1) makes that protection non-waivable. A clause making the tenant accept the unit 'as-is' or waive the (implied) warranty of habitability is unenforceable as to the landlord's statutory duties.
rules.tenant_explainer: You can't sign away your right to a livable home. 'Tenant accepts the unit as-is' or 'waives the warranty of habitability' doesn't let the landlord off the hook for heat, hot water, and code-level repairs.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7(a) — landlord must keep premises fit and habitable
citations.quote: A landlord shall: … (2) make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition ….

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(1) & (b) — waiver prohibited; provision unenforceable
citations.quote: A rental agreement shall not provide that the tenant: (1) Agrees to waive or forfeit rights or remedies under this chapter … (b) A provision prohibited by subsection (a) of this section … is unenforceable.
